questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U06_L07_GP01

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.CGM.11

A plane slices a cylinder parallel to its circular bases. What cross-section is formed?

feedback.text: A slice parallel to the circular bases has the same circular shape.
A cylinder does not form a triangle from a base-parallel slice.
A perpendicular slice may form a rectangle, but not this slice.
A parabola is a conic section, not this cylinder cross-section.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U06_L07_GP02

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.CGM.12

Rotating a rectangle around one side creates which solid?

feedback.text: A cone comes from rotating a right triangle around a leg.
A rectangle rotated around one side sweeps out a cylinder.
A sphere can come from rotating a semicircle.
A pyramid is not created by rotating a rectangle around one side.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U06_L07_GP03

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.CGM.16

Which conic section can be formed by slicing a cone parallel to its base?

feedback.text: A parabola comes from a different angled slice.
A base-parallel slice is specifically circular.
A slice parallel to the cone base forms a circle.
A cone slice can form curves, not only a line segment.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U06_L07_GP04

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.CGM.11

Which statement best supports a cross-section conclusion?

feedback.text: Appearance alone is not enough evidence.
Shading may help visualize but does not identify the slice.

answer.text: The answer is always a circle

feedback.text: Different solids and slicing directions create different shapes.

answer.text: The shape depends on the solid and the direction of the slice

feedback.text: Cross-sections are determined by both the solid and slicing plane.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U06_L07_GP05

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.CGM.12

Rotating a semicircle around its diameter creates which object?

feedback.text: A semicircle rotated around its diameter sweeps out a sphere.
A cylinder comes from rotating a rectangle.
A cone comes from rotating a right triangle.
A prism is not created by this rotation.
